narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Today will feel slightly warmer with calmer winds and dry again. While land areas across Kisumu will remain dry through the daytime, convective instability spikes tonight peaking around 20:00, where models disagree significantly—UKMO builds high CAPE (2390 J/kg) supporting localized thunder potential, whereas GFS (200 J/kg) and ECMWF (390 J/kg) keep instability modest.

## Today's Forecast
Conditions across Kisumu will stay dry and warm through the day with 0.0 mm (0.00 in) of precipitation expected onshore. Temperatures will rise from a morning low of 20°C / 68°F to a daytime high of 32°C / 90°F to 33°C / 91°F. Winds will start light from the northeast at 5-10 km/h (3-5 kt) before shifting southwesterly in the afternoon at 15-22 km/h (8-12 kt) from the SW/W, with peak gusts reaching up to 32 km/h (17 kt). The peak UV index will reach 9.2 (Very High) around midday (12:00-13:00 EAT), requiring sun protection. Current ground air quality sensors at Kisumu Airport, Ochieng' Avenue, and Dunga Beach are all stale (3 hours old, last valid reading AQI 46 at Dunga Beach), so current air quality assessment relies on CAMS model guidance, which estimates a US AQI of 78 to 87 (Moderate) throughout the day.

## Extended Outlook
Days 1-3 (Sep 5 - Sep 7): Warm, sunny conditions continue through Friday (Sep 5) and Saturday (Sep 6) with maximum temperatures of 33°C / 91°F to 35°C / 95°F and daily rain sums near 0.0 mm (0.00 in). A synoptic pattern change arrives on Sunday, September 7th (Day+3): ECMWF (3.7 mm / 0.15 in, 83% probability) and ICON (2.1 mm / 0.08 in, 65% probability) bring returning afternoon showers and cooler highs near 31°C / 88°F, while GFS stays dry.

Days 4-7 (Sep 8 - Sep 11): Rain potential increases across the Nyanza Basin next week. ECMWF projects scattered showers and thunderstorms on September 8th and 10th (up to 4.0 mm / 0.16 in), bringing daytime highs down to 28°C / 82°F – 32°C / 90°F. GFS delays rain onset until September 11th (2.0 mm / 0.08 in). Note that at Day+7, GFS holds an 82% rain verification record compared to ECMWF's 71%.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe weather hazards are expected onshore in Kisumu during daytime hours. Elevated convective energy late this evening (peaking around 20:00 EAT) brings a minor potential for isolated lightning near the lake shoreline. Sunburn risk is high under a peak UV index of 9.2 between 11:00 and 15:00 EAT.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Over open lake waters, winds will run light easterly at 5-10 km/h (3-5 kt) at dawn, turning southwesterly at 15-20 km/h (8-11 kt) by late afternoon, with gusts up to 25 km/h (13 kt) from the SW. Although onshore areas stay dry, lake-level convective instability is remarkably strong overnight and through early morning hours: CAPE values reach 1600-2300 J/kg on ECMWF and up to 3400 J/kg on UKMO. Boaters and night fishermen should prepare for sudden nocturnal thunderstorm development, gusty squalls, and localized rough water over open waters through dawn.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1003 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1017 hPa) — a 14 hPa spread, establishing a strong large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the northeast is filling over the next three days while pressure overhead remains near-steady. On the regional basin scale, mean sea-level pressure across Nyanza Basin points ranges from 1011.3 hPa at Kisumu to 1013.6 hPa in higher terrain to the south, with a mild 24-hour pressure drop of ~1.0 hPa today. This regional pressure tendency combined with solar heating drives local lake-land breeze circulations and nighttime convective buildup over the lake.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecaster confidence for today's dry onshore call is high, as all numerical models (GFS, ECMWF, ICON, UKMO) and Kenya Met agree on zero measurable rainfall across Kisumu. Kenya Met forecasts a high of 32.0°C / low of 20.0°C with sunny intervals, agreeing fully with the numerical consensus.

Regarding model performance: at Day+0, Long-Run Review findings confirm Best Match is the strongest rain caller (88% accuracy across 24 checks) while GFS is the weakest (67%). Furthermore, GFS systematically over-forecasts peak surface winds by +21.5 km/h at Day+0 (+23.7 km/h over the last 10 checks), whereas ECMWF (+10.0 km/h error) and ICON (+8.6 km/h error) provide superior wind guidance. ICON exhibits a known nocturnal cold bias (-2.5°C all-time, -2.8°C recent 10-check), and UKMO shows a warm low bias (+1.5°C). Guidance recency floor is 9.0 hours old (cycle 2026-09-03T18:00Z).

Individual ground AQI station readings from midnight are: Kisumu Airport (A418534: AQI 42), Ochieng' Avenue (A418300: AQI 31), and Dunga Beach (A418504: AQI 46). All three readings are 3 hours old (stale), so current air quality assessment relies on CAMS model guidance (US AQI ~81-87, Moderate).
